content.text:
h12.

**Answer: `(*sqlite.DB).CreateMemo` — `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/memo.go:16` (the INSERT statement is built at line 41 and executed at line 42); determined by tracing the `store.Driver` interface dispatch back to the compile-time-fixed default of the `--driver` flag.**

## The candidates

Three concrete types implement `store.Driver.CreateMemo` (`store/driver.go:29`), and each emits its own INSERT:

| Implementation | Path | SQL flavor |
|---|---|---|
| sqlite | `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:41` | `` INSERT INTO `memo` … RETURNING `id`, … `` |
| postgres | `store/db/postgres/memo.go:38` | `INSERT INTO memo … RETURNING id, …` (`$N` placeholders) |
| mysql | `store/db/mysql/memo.go:41` | `` INSERT INTO `memo` … `` (no RETURNING; uses `LastInsertId`) |

Static call-graph analysis alone cannot pick between them — the call site `s.driver.CreateMemo(ctx, create)` in `store/memo.go:113` is an interface method, so the target is only fixed at runtime by which struct was stored in `Store.driver`.

## How I resolved which one runs

I followed the value, not the types:

1. **Call chain to the interface.** `CreateMemo` RPC handler → `s.Store.CreateMemo(ctx, create)` at `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:115` → `(*Store).CreateMemo` at `store/memo.go:109-114`, which does a UID regex check and delegates straight to `s.driver.CreateMemo`. No caching or decorator layer intervenes — `store.New` (`store/store.go:37-60`) stores the driver verbatim; its three caches are for instance settings, users, and user settings only.

2. **Where `driver` is assigned.** `store.New(dbDriver, instanceProfile)` in `cmd/memos/main.go:64`, with `dbDriver` produced by `db.NewDBDriver(instanceProfile)` at line 57.

3. **The switch that selects it.** `db.NewDBDriver` (`store/db/db.go:14-32`) branches on `profile.Driver`: `"sqlite"` → `sqlite.NewDB`, `"mysql"`, `"postgres"`, else error `"unknown db driver"`.

4. **The default value of `profile.Driver`.** `Driver: viper.GetString("driver")` (`cmd/memos/main.go:43`), and the default is `"sqlite"` — set twice, at `viper.SetDefault("driver", "sqlite")` (line 122) and as the flag default in `rootCmd.PersistentFlags().String("driver", "sqlite", …)` (line 130). Note the `default:` case returns an error rather than falling back, so "no flags" only works because a non-empty default exists.

5. **Default install is viable without a DSN too.** `Profile.Validate` (`internal/profile/profile.go`) fills in a DSN specifically for this case: when `p.Driver == "sqlite" && p.DSN == ""` it sets `p.DSN = <dataDir>/memos_prod.db` (`memos_demo.db` in demo mode). This matters because `sqlite.NewDB` (`store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:26-28`) errors out with `"dsn required"` on an empty DSN — so the sqlite path is the only one that self-configures with zero flags; mysql/postgres would fail immediately.

**Corroborating check:** the sqlite build carries no build tags or alternate file variants (`store/db/sqlite/memo.go` starts plainly with `package sqlite`), so there is exactly one `(*sqlite.DB).CreateMemo` in the binary. A useful runtime tell if you want to confirm on a live instance: only the sqlite and postgres versions use `RETURNING`, and only sqlite uses backquoted identifiers together with `?` placeholders — mysql omits `RETURNING` entirely.
